provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: THE 1862 TEXT LAYER HAS NO 'da' BEFORE 'populis tuis'. Line 44265 ends 'unius efficis voluntatis:' and line 44266 begins 'populis tuis id amare quod'.; 1862 sets a colon after 'promittis'; the 1962 sets a semicolon. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 44658-44663: line 44659 ends 'vnius cfficie voluntatis' and 44660 begins 'odpopulistuis id amare quod', i.e. a two-letter word stands before 'populis tuis' at exactly this place and is recognised as 'od' for 'da'. Recorded limitation: A WORD IS ABSENT FROM THE 1862 LAYER AND WAS NOT SILENTLY REPAIRED. The 1862's line break falls exactly where 'da' would sit, at the end of 44265, which is the pattern the lane brief describes for a word lost to an OCR line break; but unlike the Quinquagesima case there is no visible fragment at all, only the gap. The 1570 supplies a word there and the Benziger 1962 reads 'da populis tuis'. On that evidence I record the prayer as matched at medium confidence, and the reviewer should know that the 1862 alone does not carry the verb.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui fidelium mentes unius efficis voluntatis: da populis tuis id amare
quod praecipis, id desiderare quod promittis; ut inter mundanas varietates
ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gaudia. Per Dominum.

It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
